data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains rather than describes its subject when the subject's observable surface is itself a product of the test's own registry, so the test can only describe what the registry has already decided to expose; the 3-of-26 result is the registry's decision boundary, not the subject's failure rate.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the 3-of-26 survivors can be observed through an interface that does not go through the registry, and they still survive, the registry-boundary mechanism fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 1-of-9 compile.py survivor's observable surface is entirely independent of the registry, its survival is trivially explained but the mechanism is not general.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 4/4-to-6/7 modules have fully registry-routed surfaces and still vary, then the registry is not the sole constraint.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If a second registry with a different first-failure marking produces the same survivor set, the decision-boundary claim is weakened.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The registry is both the test's oracle and the subject's interface. When a mutation is installed shown-to-fail-first, the registry's decision to mark the first failure as canonical closes off the observable surface for later mutations. The 1-of-9 compile.py survivor is a mutation whose observable surface was not routed through the registry at all, so it escaped the constraint. The 4/4-to-6/7 modules are those whose observable surface is partially registry-routed, so their scores reflect how much of their surface the registry had already decided to hide after the first failure.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
